subject.title: fix: Windows /restart falls back to in-process restart without changing PID

question: Should env-less Windows gateway processes with an installed Scheduled Task be treated as supervised for /restart, and what exact task-name/proof contract should the linked PR satisfy before merge?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but changing the Windows fallback from in-process restart to a Scheduled Task handoff is compatibility-sensitive and already has an open PR with review concerns.

options.title: Review linked PR with exact task proof
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers require the linked PR to probe the same task name that the handoff will run and provide redacted Windows /restart plus /status proof.

options.title: Keep current in-process fallback
options.body: Decide that env-less manual Windows gateway runs are intentionally unmanaged, then close this issue and the linked PR with that product rationale.

options.title: Sponsor a broader restart recovery design
options.body: Pause the linked PR and design a larger Windows restart/doctor recovery path that handles env-less tasks, custom profiles, and fallback diagnostics together.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR with exact task proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers require the linked PR to probe the same task name that the handoff will run and provide redacted Windows /restart plus /status proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He appears in the recent restart/supervisor refactor and current-main merge history and is the best available routing candidate for the compatibility decision.
